description: What a PS2-era NCAA Football roster's 5-bit ratings mean on the 0-99 scale
the game shows the player. Every rating column in that generation -- overall,
speed, strength, awareness and the rest -- is stored in five bits, 0-31, and
the game expands it through this one shared table on the way to the screen.
MEASURED, not derived. Read off in-game screenshots of the 2004 USC roster:
nine players, four columns each (OVR, SPD, STR, AWR), matched against what
the file stores for those same players. Twenty-one of the thirty-two stored
values were observed directly and six of them were confirmed two or three
times over by different players and different columns landing on the same
number -- which is also what establishes that ONE table serves every rating
column rather than each having its own.
The curve is compressive on purpose: four points of display per step at the
bottom, then three, then two, then one at the top, so the game spends its
resolution where the difference between players matters.
Checked the other way round: putting all 7,350 named players in the file
through this table gives a league mean of 71.0 against EA's own CFB27 mean of
71.5, and puts the 2004 consensus All-Americans at the top of it -- Pollack,
Derrick Johnson, Mike Williams, Nugent, Wilkerson. Neither of those was used
to build the table, so both are evidence rather than fit.
measuredFrom: 2004 USC roster, in-game screenshots (QB and HB depth), nine players
unresolved: Reggie Bush's awareness reads 72 in-game against a stored 12, where Brandon
Hance's awareness and Rocky Hinds's overall both read 76 from that same
stored 12. One disagreement in twenty-two. 12 -> 76 is kept because two
independent players agree on it; the Bush reading is unexplained and worth
a second look if it ever matters.
